Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Regency Government is the Regent as an element of regional government organizer who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 6. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, spiritual mental, social, knowledge and skills capabilities so that Women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to someone's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering in someone. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with other people for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is someone who neglects a person within their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefit, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or causing a person to be exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial and/or all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution or indecency activities. jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 4

20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in the emergence of misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household environment. 21. Family is a person who has blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

Article 29

(1) The Regent in implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women as referred to in Article 28 undertakes efforts to:

a. coordinate implementation among Regional Apparatus; b. cooperate with the central government, provincial government, and other regency/city governments in accordance with the provisions of legislation;
c. strengthen gender institutional capacity;
d. facilitate services for the Protection of Women; e. provide services for the Protection of Women; f. implement affirmative action for the Protection of Women; and
g. develop a data collection system for the Protection of Women including a data collection system for Violence Against Women.
(2) The implementation of policies, programs, and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Vice Regent.

Article 36

(1) The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in Article 35 consists of Victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, Repatriation assistance, or other forms.

(2) The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including Victims of Human Trafficking, Women in disaster-prone areas, working Women, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, Women Victims of sexual exploitation, Women heads of households, and Women in other vulnerable groups.

Article 48

This Regional Regulation shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 31

The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 25 letter c and letter d are in the form of full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women as family members.

Article 40

(1) The Regional Government establishes a forum for the protection of women victims of violence at every sub-district level.

(2) The forum for the protection of women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to:

a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of protection services for women victims of violence; b. facilitate and provide more optimal services and reach lower-level communities; c. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
d. compile a database regarding the development of protection for women victims of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, membership composition, duties, and functions of the Protection Forum for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) are stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 19

(1) The implementation of Protection for domestic women workers in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.

(2) Domestic women workers as referred to in paragraph (1) are entitled to protection over:

a. recognition of rights, wages, and decent working conditions; b. health insurance and social security;
c. access to information and legal consultation services; and d. opportunities to acquire knowledge and skills to improve economic status.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions of men and Women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development. 27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women. 28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and normally both in the family and in society. 29. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 5

31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance. 33. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

Article 11

(1) Women have the right to receive health services in order to lead a healthy, safe reproductive and sexual life, free from coercion and/or violence.

(2) Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. health services during the pre-pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum periods;
b. pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health; and
c. reproductive health services.
d. health services implemented through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches. jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 9

CHAPTER VII

PREVENTION, PROTECTION SERVICES, AND RECOVERY OF WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 27

(1) The Regent integrates policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women into regional development planning.

(2) The integration of programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is set forth in planning and budget documents which include:

a. regional long-term development plan; b. regional medium-term development plan; c. strategic plan of Regional Apparatus;
d. regional government work plan; and
e. work plan and budget of Regional Apparatus work units.
(3) The Regional Apparatus responsible for Women facilitates the integration of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women into the preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (2).
(4) In carrying out activities as referred to in paragraph (3) the Regional Apparatus responsible for Women coordinates with Regional Apparatus that have direct relations with the field of Women.

Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 6. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, spiritual mental, social, knowledge and skills capabilities so that Women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Domestic Neglect is someone who neglects a person within their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 31

The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 25 letter c and letter d are in the form of full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women as family members.

Article 36

(1) The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in Article 35 consists of Victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, Repatriation assistance, or other forms.

(2) The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including Victims of Human Trafficking, Women in disaster-prone areas, working Women, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, Women Victims of sexual exploitation, Women heads of households, and Women in other vulnerable groups.

(1) The Regent in implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women as referred to in Article 28 undertakes efforts to:

a. coordinate implementation among Regional Apparatus; b. cooperate with the central government, provincial government, and other regency/city governments in accordance with the provisions of legislation;
c. strengthen gender institutional capacity;
d. facilitate services for the Protection of Women; e. provide services for the Protection of Women; f. implement affirmative action for the Protection of Women; and
g. develop a data collection system for the Protection of Women including a data collection system for Violence Against Women.
(2) The implementation of policies, programs, and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Vice Regent.

Article 40

(1) The Regional Government establishes a forum for the protection of women victims of violence at every sub-district level.

(2) The forum for the protection of women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to:

a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of protection services for women victims of violence; b. facilitate and provide more optimal services and reach lower-level communities; c. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
d. compile a database regarding the development of protection for women victims of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, membership composition, duties, and functions of the Protection Forum for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) are stipulated by Regent Decree.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 31

The obligations of the family and parents as referred to in Article 25 letter c and letter d are in the form of full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women as family members.

Article 20

(1) The implementation of protection for women as economic pillars of the family in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women as economic pillars of the family.

(2) Women as economic pillars of the family as referred to in paragraph (1) are entitled to protection over:

a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as economic pillars of the family; jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 12
b. strengthening of capacities and recognition as economic pillars of the family in their environment; and c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.

Article 29

(1) The Regent in implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women as referred to in Article 28 undertakes efforts to:

a. coordinate implementation among Regional Apparatus; b. cooperate with the central government, provincial government, and other regency/city governments in accordance with the provisions of legislation;
c. strengthen gender institutional capacity;
d. facilitate services for the Protection of Women; e. provide services for the Protection of Women; f. implement affirmative action for the Protection of Women; and
g. develop a data collection system for the Protection of Women including a data collection system for Violence Against Women.
(2) The implementation of policies, programs, and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Vice Regent.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to someone's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering in someone. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with other people for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is someone who neglects a person within their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefit, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or causing a person to be exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial and/or all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution or indecency activities. jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 4

20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with other people for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is someone who neglects a person within their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefit, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or causing a person to be exploited. 19. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

a. forming family partners at the sub-district and/or village level;
b. forming women's protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting socialization of women's rights independently; d. providing first aid to victims; and e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment; (3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and the mass media.

d. facilitate services for the Protection of Women; e. provide services for the Protection of Women; f. implement affirmative action for the Protection of Women; and
g. develop a data collection system for the Protection of Women including a data collection system for Violence Against Women.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 40

(1) The Regional Government establishes a forum for the protection of women victims of violence at every sub-district level.

(2) The forum for the protection of women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duty to:

a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of protection services for women victims of violence; b. facilitate and provide more optimal services and reach lower-level communities; c. maintain and develop networks and referral systems; and
d. compile a database regarding the development of protection for women victims of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, membership composition, duties, and functions of the Protection Forum for Women Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) are stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Regency Government is the Regent as an element of regional government organizer who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a Woman. 6. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against Women. 7. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, spiritual mental, social, knowledge and skills capabilities so that Women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities. 8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily. 9. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against Women will or has occurred. 10. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to someone's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering in someone. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with other people for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is someone who neglects a person within their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefit, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or causing a person to be exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial and/or all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution or indecency activities. jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 4

20. Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in the emergence of misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household environment. 21. Family is a person who has blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

Article 36

(1) The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in Article 35 consists of Victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, Social Reintegration, Repatriation assistance, or other forms.

(2) The provision of Women's Protection services as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided for Women Victims of Violence including Victims of Human Trafficking, Women in disaster-prone areas, working Women, elderly Women, Women with disabilities, Women Victims of sexual exploitation, Women heads of households, and Women in other vulnerable groups.

Article 29

(1) The Regent in implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women as referred to in Article 28 undertakes efforts to:

a. coordinate implementation among Regional Apparatus; b. cooperate with the central government, provincial government, and other regency/city governments in accordance with the provisions of legislation;
c. strengthen gender institutional capacity;
d. facilitate services for the Protection of Women; e. provide services for the Protection of Women; f. implement affirmative action for the Protection of Women; and
g. develop a data collection system for the Protection of Women including a data collection system for Violence Against Women.
(2) The implementation of policies, programs, and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Vice Regent.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency is Pangandaran Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Pangandaran. 3. Victim is a Woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 11. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social and psychological to the victim. 12. Victim of Violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations or criminal acts as well as acts of Violence committed either by state apparatus, Regional Government apparatus, or individuals. 13. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 3 certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to someone's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death. 15. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering in someone. 16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with other people for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Domestic Neglect is someone who neglects a person within their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person. In addition, neglect also applies to anyone who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, fraud, deception, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefit, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or causing a person to be exploited. 19. Exploitation is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial and/or all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all prostitution or indecency activities. jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 4

20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

d. facilitate services for the Protection of Women; e. provide services for the Protection of Women; f. implement affirmative action for the Protection of Women; and

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CONCERNING

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

I. GENERAL

Fundamentally, the Region is formed to improve public services and realize public welfare, therefore in the implementation of autonomy, the region has obligations including protecting the community, maintaining unity, integrity and national harmony.

Unequal opportunities in all areas of life including in the fields of economy, social culture, politics and governance, law, education, health, employment and social security, may give rise to various social problems, especially for women. The reality shows that in the Region there are still acts of violence both physically, psychologically, sexually and this constitutes a violation of human rights. Violence against women is a violation of human rights so their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be addressed by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic and education levels, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing policies for the protection of women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing P2TP2A, ensuring the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking to create cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Domestic Violence is any act against a Woman that results in the emergence of misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or Domestic Neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household environment. 21. Family is a person who has blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a Woman. 22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 23. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by Women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and Women. 24. All Forms of Discrimination Against Women are all forms of discrimination that include territorial dimensions, age dimensions, and special dimensions. 25. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and Women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 26.

Gender Equality is the equality of conditions of men and Women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development. 27. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and Women. 28. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of Victims including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that Victims can carry out their roles again properly and normally both in the family and in society. 29. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return Victims of Violence to their area of origin. jdih.pangandarankab.go.id 5

31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite Victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims. 32. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to carry out the functions and main tasks of integrated services for Women and children victims of violence, including complaint services, Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, Repatriation, Social Reintegration, and legal assistance. 33. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, are performance benchmarks for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports, complaints, health services, Social Rehabilitation, enforcement and legal assistance, as well as Repatriation and Social Reintegration for Women Victims of Violence.

Article 29

(1) The Regent in implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women as referred to in Article 28 undertakes efforts to:

a. coordinate implementation among Regional Apparatus; b. cooperate with the central government, provincial government, and other regency/city governments in accordance with the provisions of legislation;
c. strengthen gender institutional capacity;
d. facilitate services for the Protection of Women; e. provide services for the Protection of Women; f. implement affirmative action for the Protection of Women; and
g. develop a data collection system for the Protection of Women including a data collection system for Violence Against Women.
